problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to service eight specialized facilities across a region. The facilities are positioned at the following grid coordinates:

Facility Alpha: (106,27)
Facility Beta: (25,143)
Facility Gamma: (123,121)
Facility Delta: (86,87)
Facility Epsilon: (31,122)
Facility Zeta: (29,179)
Facility Eta: (127,109)
Facility Theta: (9,77)

Travel distances between facilities, in kilometers, are predetermined as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 95.5 km
Alpha to Delta: 63.2 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 121.0 km
Alpha to Zeta: 170.4 km
Alpha to Eta: 84.6 km
Alpha to Theta: 109.1 km
Beta to Gamma: 100.4 km
Beta to Delta: 82.8 km
Beta to Epsilon: 21.8 km
Beta to Zeta: 36.2 km
Beta to Eta: 107.5 km
Beta to Theta: 67.9 km
Gamma to Delta: 50.2 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 92.0 km
Gamma to Zeta: 110.5 km
Gamma to Eta: 12.6 km
Gamma to Theta: 122.2 km
Delta to Epsilon: 65.2 km
Delta to Zeta: 108.2 km
Delta to Eta: 46.5 km
Delta to Theta: 77.6 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 57.0 km
Epsilon to Eta: 96.9 km
Epsilon to Theta: 50.1 km
Zeta to Eta: 120.4 km
Zeta to Theta: 103.9 km
Eta to Theta: 122.3 km

Direct travel between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta is not possible due to a geographical barrier. Furthermore, due to contractual obligations with local authorities, the technician's route must incorporate exactly one of two specific critical links: either the connection between Beta and Gamma, or the connection between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a circuit that services each facility precisely once before returning to the point of origin.
